title: `AudioStreamWAV`: Make loop points consistent in importer and mixer
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve? - Partially reverts #96768 and fully reverts #110515 - Closes #119778 - Prevents a crash in one case with `AudioStreamWAV::load_from_buffer()`. Before #96768, the mixer's `end_limit` would always be treated as inclusive even when not looping. The reason it wouldn't have an audible pop was because of [silent data pads at the beginning and end](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e4becfb0a1a8423d3bbc6fd7afcfeee4fd840b13/scene/resources/audio_stream_wav.cpp#L502). While #96768 "fixed" having an extra frame by pointing `loop_end` to the last frame from import instead of one after, #110482 revealed that `loop_end` can, and usually in some files with baked loops, ***is*** placed in the frame past the end, meaning the previous PR was a broken workaround rather than a fix. And on top of that workaround, another workaround had to be done (#110515). Those workarounds aren't 100% the reason #119778 exists, but I believe they make the issue worse and keeping them isn't right, so I opted to undo them, while making `loop_end` exclusive in all situations (`end_limit` now subtracts 1 from it, like it does with `len`), so a frame "stored" there will never be reached. This ensures no more loop frames get skipped.

While the `loop_end = frames - 1` case mismatches differently from before, it does not skip `loop_begin` anymore. In fact, it should be the intended behavior since `loop_end = frames` is now considered the correct case and I don't think it's possible for them to co-exist. I also re-tested the MRP from #110482 to make sure the crash wouldn't come back. ## Another problem found while testing While developing and testing this PR, I was trying random values in the Loop End field, and found out the Loop Begin and Loop End fields are unlocked for values way beyond the end. And they will be accepted: This causes the audio to stop playing, with a loud pop if it's PCM. But, with Quite OK Audio and a number of samples lower than 5120 (maximum number of samples in a QOA frame, same situation as #110482), it will outright **crash** the engine as it tries to get an index out of bounds (yes, second screenshot above was taken during a crash). I have placed a `MIN()` to make sure this can't happen anymore. Could be a separate PR, but since this touches loop points, I think it's better to have it here. ## Additional information Any files imported with Loop Mode set to Forward, Ping-Pong or Backward and Loop End set to `-1` may need to be reimported to take the excluded last frame. Otherwise it's a pretty much inaudible artifact and should not be dangerous. 🧍 **Human disclosure**: This contribution was completely authored by a human. No AI was used.
